A while back, I saw their call for interesting resources on the topic. 
Now, [Development Seed][ds] offers their primer on Earth data embeddings[^earth-embedding]. From 
their [blog post][post]:  

> Embeddings are one way we make use of the rich representations learned by 
geospatial foundation models[^gfm], supporting everything from search and retrieval 
to natural language interfaces. Yet for many practitioners, the concept remains 
opaque. This primer explores how embeddings are generated, the kinds of 
questions they help answer, and why they’re useful across the geospatial 
ecosystem.

The Development Seed team has made available both [a poster][poster] and a 
[zine][zine][^zine]. The aforementioned [blog post][post] shows animated 
pieces and graphics from the latter.

![A high-level workflow diagram of building and using Earth data embeddings (source: [Development Seed][post])](embeddings-workflow.png "A high-level workflow diagram of building and using Earth data embeddings (source: Development Seed)")

This looks very promising. Last year, Development Seed published a [zine on 
cloud-native][cn][^cloud-native] the quality of which I appreciated.


[^earth-embedding]: A geospatial embedding is a compact, high-dimensional vector representation of a geospatial location, scene, or feature, learned so that similar places or patterns end up close together in vector space.
[^gfm]: Geospatial foundation models are large AI models pre-trained on vast amounts of Earth observation and other geospatial data, which can then be adapted to many downstream tasks.
[^zine]: "Zine" is short for "magazine".
[^cloud-native]: I.e., taking full advantage of the cloud computing model; in the data world typically through enabling partial downloads of file contents through so-called [HTTP range requests](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Range_requests).
